name: Facet
text:
Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags low-contrast elements in real time, so the team sees violations immediately—not after a build or review. This forces ownership: designers fix issues on the spot, keeping the interface vivid and readable.

Trade-off: it adds a small runtime cost to every design tweak, but that’s outweighed by the clarity and speed gains.

name: Pane
text: The live checker trains designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt alarms—it turns contrast into noise. A pre-submit gate, not a live checker, makes contrast a real constraint: designers must fix it before shipping, not just when they remember. The argument settles when we measure how often low-contrast elements escape into production with each approach.

name: Facet
text:
Ship a pre-submit contrast gate that blocks builds with insufficient contrast. It treats contrast like a hard constraint, not a suggestion—designers must fix violations before shipping, not just when they notice them. The trade-off is slower iteration: a failed build forces a fix before moving forward. But this guarantees the interface stays vivid and readable, which aligns with our goal of clarity and enjoyment.

name: Pane
text: The pre-submit gate turns contrast into a blocker that kills momentum when the team is hot—designers will game the system by tweaking values just enough to pass, not to improve. Instead, ship the live checker but pair it with a "contrast debt" tracker in the interface: every violation stays visible until fixed, and we measure how long issues linger. Settle it by tracking designer response time to live warnings versus pre-submit blocks—if the former reduces debt faster, the live checker wins.
